summary: Show local IPv4 and IPv6 enodes in peer status
details: Peer status and watch reuse the existing endpoint inspection to show local address candidates, applied and pending families, and local probe failures separately from network membership.
JSON status adds a local endpoint report. Connected peer text includes the actual remote socket address, and acknowledged first nodes no longer receive an unnecessary add-seed hint.

Reuse the validated chain observation without a second chain RPC probe; suppress local candidates when identity is unavailable or transport changes are pending, and retain explicit public reachability limits.
Add an operator handbook chapter covering enode export, IPv6 and dual-stack configuration, seed connection verification, and legacy release limitations.
operator_actions: Use peers status or peers status --watch to inspect local enodes after installing a release containing this display change. Existing IPv6-capable releases can export the same candidates with peers enode --family ipv6.
Verify IPv6 routing in the chain container and actual peer connections; an IPv6 route on the host alone does not upgrade an older IPv4-only deployment.
